latest_teacher_action.diagnosis: The first prompt preserved the trucks well, but the pig and cow groups were too weakly specified as distinct, prominent, countable subjects. 'Separate clearly visible group' for cows was not enough to force recognizable cows, and 'glass pigs' likely rendered as ambiguous pig-like sculptures that were not reliably detected as pigs or counted as four. The plan also spread attention across three groups without giving the failed groups a rigid layout, so the model likely under-emphasized cows and the glass material on pigs.
expected_improvement: Increase recognizability of the four pigs by making them four separate full-body glass pigs in one explicit row.
Increase recognizability and presence of the six cows by making them six separate full-body white cows in one explicit row.
Preserve the already-correct truck count, wooden attribute, and behind-the-pigs relation while simplifying the overall layout for verifier-friendly detection.
preserve_constraints: The trucks are behind the pigs.

previous_plan_error.details: The previous prompt used a broad multi-group composition but did not anchor the pigs and cows in a strict countable arrangement. It also did not make the glass material on the pigs visually explicit enough for reliable pig detection plus material binding, and it left the cows as a secondary separate group that may have been omitted or rendered ambiguously.

latest_teacher_action.regeneration_strategy: Use a simple studio-like side view with three horizontal rows and all objects fully visible. Put four glass pigs in the front row, four wooden trucks directly behind them in the middle row, and six white cows in a third row below and separate from the pig-truck rows. Require full-body, evenly spaced, non-overlapping instances so each pig and each cow is individually countable and recognizable. Emphasize transparent glass material only on the pigs and white color only on the cows.
regression_risks: The generator may drop or blur cows if they are treated as a distant background group.
Glass pigs may become generic glass statues unless the prompt binds both pig identity and transparent glass material explicitly.
Adding many objects can cause merging or missed counts unless spacing and full-body visibility are stated clearly.
repair_constraints: Show exactly four pigs, as four separate full-body pigs.
Bind the material to the pigs: each of the four pigs is made of transparent glass.
Show exactly six cows, as six separate full-body cows.
Bind the color to the cows: each of the six cows is white.
Keep all pigs and cows large enough, unobstructed, and clearly recognizable for counting.
Maintain exactly four wooden trucks behind the pigs.
latest_teacher_action.retry_prompt: Create a clear image of exactly fourteen subjects arranged in three separate horizontal rows, all fully visible and easy to count. Front row: exactly four separate full-body pigs made of transparent glass, evenly spaced, side view, clearly recognizable as pigs. Middle row, directly behind the pigs: exactly four separate wooden trucks, evenly spaced, each truck behind a pig. Bottom row as a separate row: exactly six separate full-body white cows, evenly spaced, clearly recognizable as cows. Keep every truck, pig, and cow unobstructed, non-overlapping, and visually distinct. Preserve the relation that the four wooden trucks are behind the four glass pigs. Do not include any extra trucks, pigs, cows, or any other prominent objects.

skill_revision.reason: Persistent failures show that generic multi-object composition was too loose. The retry should focus more on rigid countable layout, object presence, attribute binding, and visibility, with less emphasis on broad scene composition and more on verifier-friendly rows of distinct instances.

retry_ready_action.diagnosis: The first prompt preserved the trucks well, but the pig and cow groups were too weakly specified as distinct, prominent, countable subjects. 'Separate clearly visible group' for cows was not enough to force recognizable cows, and 'glass pigs' likely rendered as ambiguous pig-like sculptures that were not reliably detected as pigs or counted as four. The plan also spread attention across three groups without giving the failed groups a rigid layout, so the model likely under-emphasized cows and the glass material on pigs.
expected_improvement: Increase recognizability of the four pigs by making them four separate full-body glass pigs in one explicit row.
Increase recognizability and presence of the six cows by making them six separate full-body white cows in one explicit row.
Preserve the already-correct truck count, wooden attribute, and behind-the-pigs relation while simplifying the overall layout for verifier-friendly detection.
preserve_constraints: The trucks are behind the pigs.

previous_plan_error.details: The previous prompt used a broad multi-group composition but did not anchor the pigs and cows in a strict countable arrangement. It also did not make the glass material on the pigs visually explicit enough for reliable pig detection plus material binding, and it left the cows as a secondary separate group that may have been omitted or rendered ambiguously.

retry_ready_action.regeneration_strategy: Use a simple studio-like side view with three horizontal rows and all objects fully visible. Put four glass pigs in the front row, four wooden trucks directly behind them in the middle row, and six white cows in a third row below and separate from the pig-truck rows. Require full-body, evenly spaced, non-overlapping instances so each pig and each cow is individually countable and recognizable. Emphasize transparent glass material only on the pigs and white color only on the cows.
regression_risks: The generator may drop or blur cows if they are treated as a distant background group.
Glass pigs may become generic glass statues unless the prompt binds both pig identity and transparent glass material explicitly.
Adding many objects can cause merging or missed counts unless spacing and full-body visibility are stated clearly.
repair_constraints: Show exactly four pigs, as four separate full-body pigs.
Bind the material to the pigs: each of the four pigs is made of transparent glass.
Show exactly six cows, as six separate full-body cows.
Bind the color to the cows: each of the six cows is white.
Keep all pigs and cows large enough, unobstructed, and clearly recognizable for counting.
Maintain exactly four wooden trucks behind the pigs.
